short: Trainable audio-visual master (M02) is new but shown on one LRS2 run; confidence curriculum (M03) adds 0.1-1.1 WER points; the state-of-the-art claim holds only against no-LM rows.
position: The paper [@ren2021master] changes the teacher (M02), a trainable audio-visual "master" updated from a temporary student, and the sample order (M03), a tutor-confidence curriculum. Before 2020-12, none of 221 lip-reading decoders updates a teacher from student feedback (pattern match, Appendix); the design is new, but its isolating comparison is one LRS2 value per row, so it stays standard. The curriculum is standard: earlier decoders already order by length, contrary to §3.4, and the gain falls to 0.1 WER points on the strongest backend (inference), as the authors concede. The strongest confound: a same-structure video teacher alone gives about half the gain of the best master setting (57.5% to 53.4% WER against 49.6%, Tables 1 and 5). The state-of-the-art claim (M12) holds only against no-LM rows [@afouras2018deep] [@shillingford2018] [@ma2020towards].
